# Plan: Prepare agentshark for OSS Release

## Context

agentshark is a pre-alpha TUI tool ("Wireshark + top for AI agents") that provides event-level introspection of AI agent sessions. The codebase is solid and well-designed but lacks the scaffolding required for an open-source release: no standalone LICENSE file, no CONTRIBUTING/CODE_OF_CONDUCT/SECURITY files, no CI/CD, a broken `npm test` path, and the README doesn't explain what users actually _see_ in the UI (header columns, event list columns, filter syntax, etc.).

---

## What Needs to Be Done

### 1. LICENSE file (root)
`package.json` says MIT but no `LICENSE` file exists. Add `LICENSE` at root with MIT full text (year: 2025, holder: the author).

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/LICENSE`

---

### 2. CONTRIBUTING.md
Standard contributor guide.

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/CONTRIBUTING.md`

Content:
- Prerequisites: Node.js 20+, npm 10+
- Clone and install: `git clone ... && npm install`
- Dev workflow: `npm run dev -- inspect`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run smoke`
- Monorepo structure overview (packages/tui, schema, redact)
- How to add a new adapter (point to `packages/tui/src/adapters/`)
- PR guidelines (test with smoke test, typecheck passes)
- Commit style (conventional commits)

---

### 3. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
Standard Contributor Covenant v2.1.

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`

---

### 4. SECURITY.md
Security disclosure policy.

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/SECURITY.md`

Content:
- Scope: redaction engine, local data handling, export format
- How to report: private email or GitHub Security Advisory
- What to include in a report
- Privacy-related: note the project's privacy guarantees

---

### 5. Fix `npm test` path bug

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/package.json`

Current (broken):
```json
"test": "node --test packages/*/test/*.js"
```

Fix: the smoke test lives in `packages/tui/scripts/smoke-test.js`, not `packages/*/test/*.js`. Also create a `packages/tui/test/` directory with a proper Node test runner entry that delegates to the smoke test (or rename the glob to `packages/*/scripts/smoke-test.js`). Simplest fix:
```json
"test": "node packages/tui/scripts/smoke-test.js"
```

---

### 6. GitHub Actions CI

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/ci.yml`

Steps on push/PR to main:
1. `npm ci` 
2. `npm run typecheck`
3. `npm run build` (build all packages)
4. Skip smoke test in CI (requires real Claude Code sessions on disk) — annotate why

Also add:
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md`** — bug report template
- **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md`** — feature request template
- **`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`** — PR checklist

---

### 7. README.md — Major Expansion

**File:** `/Users/dev/projects/example/README.md`

The current README has a pitch and basic commands but _doesn't explain what you see in the UI_. Add these sections:

#### a) Installation & Quick Start
```bash
# Run without installing (when npm published)
npx agentshark

# From source
git clone https://github.com/YOUR_ORG/agentshark
cd agentshark && npm install
npm run dev -- top        # session list
npm run dev -- inspect    # event inspector
```

#### b) `agentshark top` — Column Reference
The session list shows one row per running/recent agent session:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `PID` | OS process ID of the agent process |
| `AGENT` | Agent type (claude-code, codex, cursor, gemini-cli, copilot-cli) |
| `MODEL` | Last model used (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-6`) |
| `HOST` | Hostname (for remote sessions via collector) |
| `CTX` | Context window fill % — how full the context window is |
| `RATE` | Input token rate (tokens/min) for the current turn |

**Keyboard controls in `top`:**
- `↑/↓` — navigate sessions
- `Enter` — open selected session in `inspect` view
- `q` / `Ctrl+C` — quit

#### c) `agentshark inspect` — Three-Pane UI Reference

##### Header bar fields:
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `agentshark inspect` | Mode label |
| `[live]` / `[paused]` | Live-tailing vs. static replay |
| Project name | Inferred from session path |
| Model | Last model seen in session |
| `N turns` | Number of assistant turns so far |
| `~Ntok avg` | Average billed input tokens per API turn |
| `last: Ntok` | Input tokens on the most recent turn |
| `N% cache` | Percentage of input tokens served from cache (green = good) |

##### Event list columns:
| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| Timestamp | Wall-clock time of the event |
| Event type badge | Color-coded type (see Event Types below) |
| Short description | Tool name, MCP server/tool, hook type, or message preview |
| `in: N` | Input tokens attributed to this event |
| `out: N` | Output tokens (for assistant messages) |
| Cache state | `[HIT]` (cache read), `[WRITE]` (cache write), blank (non-cached) |

##### Inspector pane (right panel):
Shows the full payload of the selected event: raw arguments, response body, timing, span IDs.

##### Context View (`c` key):
Breaks down input token budget by category:
- System prompt, tools/skills, conversation history, current user turn
- Shows largest single blocks consuming context

#### d) Event Type Reference

| Type | Badge | Description |
|------|-------|-------------|
| `message` | white | User, assistant, or system message turn |
| `tool_call` | yellow | Agent calls a local tool (Read, Write, Bash, etc.) |
| `tool_result` | green | Tool execution result returned to agent |
| `mcp` | magenta | MCP server request, response, or error |
| `hook` | blue | Hook fired (pre_tool, post_tool, user_prompt_submit, stop) |
| `skill` | cyan | Skill invocation |
| `system_reminder` | dim | System reminder block injected into context |
| `subagent` | bright red | Sub-agent spawned or returned |
| `api_turn` | white | Full API turn boundary with token totals |
| `cache` | green | Cache checkpoint written or read |

#### e) Filter Language Reference

The filter bar (activated with `/`) supports a Wireshark-style expression language:

```
# Filter by event type
type:tool_call
type:mcp OR type:hook

# Filter by source adapter
source:claude-code

# Filter by MCP server
mcp:gmail
mcp:filesystem

# Filter by hook type  
hook:pre_tool
hook:stop

# Filter by token count
tokens > 1000
tokens < 500

# Regex search across all fields
"pattern"
"anthropic"

# Compound expressions
type:mcp AND tokens > 500
(type:tool_call OR type:mcp) AND NOT source:cursor
```

#### f) Keyboard Shortcuts (full reference)
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `↑/↓` | Navigate event list |
| `Enter` | Expand/collapse event in inspector |
| `/` | Open filter bar |
| `Esc` | Clear filter / close inspector |
| `c` | Toggle Context Composition view |
| `p` | Pause/resume live tail |
| `e` | Export current session to `.aspark` file |
| `q` / `Ctrl+C` | Quit |

#### g) Export & Replay

```bash
# Export a session (prompts for confirmation, runs secret scan)
agentshark export --session /path/to/session --output trace.aspark

# Replay offline
agentshark inspect --replay trace.aspark
```

The `.aspark` format is a versioned JSON archive (see `schema/aspark.v1.json`).

### 8. docs/cli.md — Sync with README additions

The CLI doc already has most of this, but after updating README, ensure `docs/cli.md` is consistent (header fields, column names, filter examples). Minor updates only — no duplication.

# agentshark

**Wireshark + `top` for AI agents.** Deep, event-level introspection of what an agent is actually doing — locally (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI) and remotely (production agents, CI, multi-agent orchestrators).

`agentshark inspect` is the headline: a three-pane TUI that shows every tool call, MCP roundtrip, hook fire, sub-agent spawn, and cache event in a single session, with per-event input-token attribution.

`agentshark top` is the entry point: an `htop`-style live list of every agent session running on your machine or streaming from your collector — including multi-agent topologies as a tree.

---

## Privacy posture (read this first)

agentshark is built for a security-conscious developer audience. The rules:

1. **Local mode never sends data anywhere.** Live tail and replay run entirely on your machine, against log files the agents already wrote.
2. **Remote SDK redacts client-side, before transmission.** A built-in secret scanner (API keys, JWTs, AWS credentials, common `*_KEY` / `*_TOKEN` shapes) runs before any event leaves the agent's host. Project-specific patterns via `.agentshark-redact`.
3. **Self-hosted collector is a first-class option.** One Docker container, embedded SQLite by default. Postgres / ClickHouse pluggable for production scale. You never have to use a hosted platform.
4. **Export is explicit.** `agentshark export` produces a `.aspark` file after running the secret scan and showing you the redaction diff for confirmation. Nothing is written until you say yes.
5. **Sharing is a separate command.** `agentshark share <file.aspark>` is the only path to a hosted viewer URL. Never automatic. URLs are unguessable and revocable.

If anything in this list looks wrong on inspection, file an issue — these are non-negotiable invariants, not aspirations.

---

## Status

Pre-alpha. TUI MVP runs against local Claude Code sessions. Remote SDK + collector + multi-agent topology are in flight (see plan).

Day-1 de-risks:

- [x] Cache-aware input token attribution validated against cold + cache-heavy real Claude Code sessions. Per-turn billed-input prediction is within <10% on ~95% of turns; the failing turns are concentrated in the first 1-3 of any session (cold start, before injected reminders accumulate). Production algorithm uses reconciliation so per-block attribution sums to billed input exactly by construction — the "system overhead" (system prompt + tool defs + memory + untracked reminders) is its own bucket in the Context Composition view, sized per-turn by subtraction. Cache hit/read state doesn't affect tokenizer accuracy because the API counts the same tokens regardless. See `packages/tui/scripts/attribution-prototype.js`.
- [x] Timestamp resolution measured in local JSONL transcripts. Millisecond precision is reliable: 52% of consecutive gaps are sub-second, ms-tens digit is uniformly distributed (8.5-11.5% per bucket of 100ms). UI may show `412ms` for tool-call durations. See `packages/tui/scripts/timestamp-resolution.js`.

## Run the TUI MVP

```sh
# from the monorepo root
cd packages/tui
npm install                              # if not already done at the root

# headless smoke test (no TTY needed)
node scripts/smoke-test.js

# explore data without the TUI — useful for CI / piping to jq
node bin/agentshark.js inspect --print --session=/path/to/session.jsonl
node bin/agentshark.js inspect --print | jq 'select(.type=="mcp")'

# interactive (requires a real terminal — iTerm, Terminal.app, your normal shell)
node bin/agentshark.js                   # top view, latest sessions
node bin/agentshark.js inspect           # most recent session
node bin/agentshark.js inspect --session=/path/to/session.jsonl
node bin/agentshark.js adapters          # what adapters detect on this machine
```

In the interactive TUI:

| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| `↑` `↓` | Move selection |
| `Enter` | (top) inspect selected session |
| `/` | (inspect) edit filter expression |
| `c` | (inspect) toggle Context Composition view |
| `t` | (inspect) toggle live tail (pause / resume polling) |
| `g` / `G` | (inspect) jump to first / last event |
| `q` | back / quit |

Filter expression supports `type:`, `subtype:`, `source:`, `mcp:<server>`, `hook:<name>`, `category:`, `tokens > N`, `tokens < N`, quoted `"regex"`, and `AND` / `OR` / `NOT`.

- [ ] Codex SQLite schema snapshot + JSONL fallback
- [ ] Hook event format confirmed against real fixtures
- [ ] OTLP semantic conventions for agentshark span attributes frozen
- [ ] SDK overhead budget measured (<5% p99)
- [ ] Multi-agent topology preservation tested end-to-end

See `/Users/dev/projects/example/trying-to-get-user-robust-robin.md` for the full plan.

---

## Packages

- `packages/tui` — the `agentshark` CLI binary (TUI for `top` and `inspect`).
- `packages/sdk-node` — the Node/TypeScript instrumentation SDK (forthcoming).
- `packages/sdk-python` — the Python instrumentation SDK (forthcoming).
- `packages/collector` — the Go collector for receiving SDK events (forthcoming).
- `schema/` — the public `.aspark` export schema, versioned.
